newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary party head offers to resign over scandal.
newsitem.headline: Hungary party head offers to resign over scandal.

text.p: Ivan Peto, president of Hungary's junior ruling coalition party the Free Democrats, has offered to resign over a privatisation scandal but his party persuaded him to withdraw his proposal.

Peto, who is also leader of the party's parliamentary group, was quoted by Hungarian television on Tuesday as saying that he had offered to resign from both posts at a meeting of the party's presidium on Monday.
The presidium convinced him to withdraw his offer, saying his resignation could make Hungarians feel that the Free Democrats were responsible for the privatisation scandal.
Peto offered to resign because a member of the party had been suspected of involvement in the scandal, Hungarian television said.

The scandal over irregular payments of millions of dollars to an adviser of the state privatisation agency APV led one week ago to the sacking of trade and industry minister Tamas Suchman, a close ally of Socialist Prime Minister Gyula Horn, and the dismissal of the APV's board of directors.
The case raised tension between the Free Democrats and the Socialist Party, the senior member of the coalition.
Peto said on Saturday the coalition could split unless the Free Democrats got more influence on decisions so as to prevent further scandals.
